articles.title: RoboDoctor: Training-Free Recursive Self-Improvement for Robot Policies
articles.summary: Generalist robot policies and language-model agents provide complementary capabilities, but completing a task also requires adapting their use to the consequences of physical interaction. We study execution as a locus of adaptation: feedback guides the current action and supplies evidence for revising subsequent decisions under fixed model weights. We introduce RoboDoctor, a training-free framework that connects diagnosis, grounded action, and persistent experience across three revision targets. The harness allocates control between policy and agent; intervention determines when to assist while preserving useful policy behavior; and operation refines physical methods through observed effects. Linked experience records retain the reason for a decision, the attempted method, its outcome, and conditions for reuse. articles.title: Papers with Code is now open-source [P]
articles.summary: Papers with Code is now open-source with an Apache 2.0-license. The goal is to collaboratively create the best paper interface with the community! Over the past couple of months, I've been working with my buddies Claude and Codex on creating a website that tracks trending AI research, benchmarks and state-of-the-art (SOTA). It's a revival of the original Papers with Code website, which Meta acquired and later shut down. The website is pretty straightforward: - Python FastAPI backend - React frontend The app itself is hosted on a Hetzner Virtual Private Server (VPS). The code is also hosted there as a single monorepo. The frontend mostly calls various API endpoints to visualize papers. The API itself is also publicly available, as is an accompanying MCP server. I've been getting cool feature requests lately, so rather than just working on it myself, I thought it would make a lot more sense to share the codebase openly so anyone can contribute. Code: https://github.com/huggingface/papers

articles.title: Give your AI agent one MCP connector to your whole workspace
articles.summary: Most AI agents start their first day the way a new hire does: one login for the task tracker, another for the docs, another for call recordings, another for customer feedback. Every extra tool is another token to manage, another set of permissions to reason about, and another place where the agent's picture of the work goes stale. This tutorial connects an agent to all four through one hosted MCP server and one API key, using Dutify. It takes about five minutes.
